reason: Full material read; in scope as A-type memory/playbook (insight list + retrieved success trajectories) retained across tasks without weight updates.

paper.title: ExpeL: LLM Agents Are Experiential Learners
paper.central_claim: An LLM agent that gathers experience on training tasks, extracts natural-language insights (success/failure contrast with ADD/EDIT/UPVOTE/DOWNVOTE) and retrieves similar successful trajectories can improve single-attempt performance on unseen tasks of HotpotQA, ALFWorld and WebShop without parameter updates, improves as experience accumulates, and transfers insights to FEVER.

provenance.notes: actual_model/session_id/receipt_ref are not exposed to the worker agent; model_type follows the claude-kimi type overlay (haiku slot -> claude-sonnet-5-5[1m]) as dispatched by the controller.

rationale: 留存洞察与相似成功轨迹在不相交折上提升ReAct(28→39,40→59)，消融较充分；仅gpt-3.5、小折、无预算匹配/方差/维护与improver证据，涌现能力仅轶事。

missing_sections: Figures 5, 6, 25-27 (main-result bars, experience-scaling curve, outcome breakdowns) are not rendered in the text extraction; their numbers were not used except where restated in prose/tables

evidence.quote: Our agent autonomously gathers experiences and extracts knowledge using natural language from a collection of training tasks.
evidence.support_explanation: Central claim: self-gathered experience becomes natural-language knowledge without parameter updates.

evidence.locator: Sec 4.2 Learning from Successes and Failures
evidence.quote: First, we let the agent compare a failed trajectory with a successful trajectory for the same task.
evidence.support_explanation: Insight extraction contrasts success/failure pairs (and lists of L successes) from the training pool.

evidence.quote: A newly added insight will have an initial importance count of two associated with it
evidence.support_explanation: Insight maintenance is ADD/EDIT/UPVOTE/DOWNVOTE with an importance counter.

evidence.quote: If an insight’s importance count reaches zero, it will be removed.
evidence.support_explanation: Only retention/forgetting rule for insights: vote-count removal, no measured utility test.

evidence.quote: we propose experience recall to retrieve successful trajectories from the experience pool gathered during training based on task similarity.
evidence.support_explanation: Second retained artifact: kNN-retrieved successful trajectories used as few-shot examples.

evidence.quote: During the evaluation stage, the agent attempts unseen tasks with a single try, augmented with extracted insights and successful trajectories in its experience pool gathered from the training stage.
evidence.support_explanation: Evaluation is a single attempt with the store frozen from training; Alg. 3 does not append to the pool.

evidence.quote: We train on one half of the dataset and evaluate on the other half, and vice versa.
evidence.support_explanation: Train/eval split of tasks per fold; construction and evaluation streams are disjoint.

evidence.quote: we utilized the 134 solvable tasks that ReAct and Reflexion used
evidence.support_explanation: Dataset sizes are 100 / 134 / 100 tasks, so each train or eval half is roughly 50-67 tasks.

evidence.quote: ExpeL matches Reflexion’s performance (40% at R3 vs. 39%) for HotpotQA and even outperforms it for ALFWorld (54% at R3 vs. 59%)
evidence.support_explanation: Single-attempt ExpeL compared with Reflexion after three retries; author report.

evidence.quote: (36%/31% and 50%/55% for HotpotQA and ALFWorld, respectively)
evidence.support_explanation: Insights-only / retrieve-only ablations (HotpotQA, ALFWorld) both below full ExpeL; store components are separable.

evidence.quote: As we can see, the agent that extracts insights from the existing fewshots has no advantage compared to the ReAct agent, illustrating that experience is essential for ExpeL to learn from.
evidence.support_explanation: Retained-store control: insights from few-shots alone give no gain; diverse Reflexion-gathered experience beats ReAct-only gathering.

evidence.quote: Hand-crafted insights enjoyed a performance boost over ReAct but were less effective than LLM-generated ones.
evidence.support_explanation: Alternative-insight controls (hand-crafted, +reflections, gpt-3.5 extractor) all below ExpeL.

evidence.quote: (1) learned insights by the agent are more advantageous than hand-crafted ones; (2) using reflections in addition to success/failure pairs and lists of successes is disadvantageous
evidence.support_explanation: Extraction design is ablated, but only on HotpotQA (E017).

evidence.quote: Lastly, random sampling has a significant drop in performance
evidence.support_explanation: Retrieval ablation on ALFWorld: task-similarity > reason-similarity > random.

evidence.quote: Both agents that transferred knowledge from the source domain saw performance gains.
evidence.support_explanation: HotpotQA->FEVER transfer; table: Act 58, ReAct 63, ExpeL Transfer w/o demos 65, ExpeL Transfer 70 (mean +- SE).

evidence.quote: Furthermore, since our extracted insights do not exceed the current LLM’s token limit, we can fit them into the agent’s context window.
evidence.support_explanation: No insight retrieval/consolidation at scale; whole list is concatenated into the prompt.

evidence.quote: Since insights had the most significant impact on the HotpotQA environment (Fig.
evidence.support_explanation: Insight-extraction ablations run only on HotpotQA; retrieval ablations only on ALFWorld.

evidence.quote: We empirically found that gpt-4-0613 is better than gpt-3.5-turbo-0613 at following instructions on how to use the insight extraction operators and hallucinated less.
evidence.support_explanation: Extractor is gpt-4 while actor is gpt-3.5: improver stronger than executor; extraction cost not reported.

evidence.quote: Furthermore, self-reflection methods are stateless and cannot learn cross-task insights.
evidence.support_explanation: Author-stated gap versus Reflexion (closest ancestor).

evidence.quote: All agents, including ExpeL, used gpt-3.5-turbo-0613 when performing actions during evaluation.
evidence.support_explanation: Single actor backbone; temperature 0 greedy decoding.

evidence.quote: All experiments were performed on a desktop: Intel(R) Core(TM) i9-9900K CPU @ 3.60GHz with 16 cores, 64GB RAM, and a single NVIDIA GeForce RTX 2080 Ti.
evidence.support_explanation: Compute described, but API call volume/dollar cost of Reflexion gathering and gpt-4 extraction is not.

evidence.quote: Finally, we share some additional metrics regarding step statistics and used tokens in Tab.
evidence.support_explanation: Table 6 reports tokens per trajectory (e.g. HotpotQA ReAct 1319.75 vs ExpeL 4310.06): ExpeL costs ~2-3x tokens at inference; no matched-budget baseline.

evidence.quote: This behavior is possibly encouraged by the generated insight
evidence.support_explanation: Emergent-ability explanations are hypotheses from manual trajectory inspection.

evidence.quote: The following claims were made based on (1) a deep understanding of each environment; (2) extracted insights and retrievable in-context examples; and (3) statistics
evidence.support_explanation: Mechanistic attributions rest on qualitative inspection.

evidence.quote: ReAct+Reflexion 40.3% 47.8% 52.2% 54.4% ExpeL retrieve only 54.5% 57.5% 59.7% 60.4% ExpeL+Reflexion 59.0% 60.4% 63.4% 64.2%
evidence.support_explanation: ALFWorld: retrieve-only 54.5% at R0 vs ReAct+Reflexion 40.3% at R0; ExpeL+Reflexion reaches 64.2% at R3.

evidence.quote: ReAct 28.0 ± \pm 1.4
evidence.support_explanation: HotpotQA ReAct baseline 28.0 +- 1.4 (SE over folds).

evidence.quote: ExpeL (ours) 39.0 ± \pm 1.7
evidence.support_explanation: HotpotQA ExpeL 39.0 +- 1.7.

evidence.support_explanation: ALFWorld ReAct 40.0 +- 0.3; ExpeL 59.0 +- 0.3 in the same table.

signatures.object: Natural-language insight list added to the task specification (prompt-level playbook)
signatures.information: Training-task trajectories gathered by ReAct+Reflexion (<=3 retries) with environment success/failure; gpt-4-0613 sees success/failure pairs of the same task or L=4-8 successes; no test-task access
signatures.operation: LLM applies ADD / EDIT / UPVOTE / DOWNVOTE to the running insight list (importance count starts 2, removed at 0)
signatures.output: Insight list concatenated into every evaluation prompt
signatures.conditions: Recurring task distribution; trustworthy environment reward during training; insights fit in context
signatures.feedback: Binary task success from the environment on training tasks
signatures.selection_rule: LLM-chosen edits plus vote counts; no held-out utility test of individual insights
signatures.persistence: Insight list built once after training; frozen at evaluation (Alg. 2-3)
signatures.later_use: Full list in prompt for each evaluation task
signatures.failure_boundary: Including reflections in extraction hurts (29.0); hallucinated insights; no consolidation at scale

signatures.object: Experience pool of successful trajectories used as dynamic few-shot examples
signatures.information: Successful training trajectories (reward=1) embedded by task text (all-mpnet-base-v2, Faiss kNN)
signatures.operation: Retrieve top-k successes by task similarity for each evaluation task
signatures.output: Few-shot examples replacing fixed ReAct demonstrations
signatures.conditions: Evaluation tasks resemble training tasks (ALFWorld task types); retrieval by task similarity
signatures.selection_rule: Success-only admission; kNN similarity at read time
signatures.later_use: Each evaluation task retrieves from the pool
signatures.claimed_effect: ALFWorld retrieve-only 55% vs insights-only 50% vs ExpeL 59% vs ReAct 40% (E010, E028)

signatures.object: Source-domain insights adapted to a target domain (HotpotQA->FEVER)

gap.author_gap: Finetuning LLM agents is costly and unavailable for closed models; prompting agents keep no memory across tasks; Reflexion improves only within a repeated task.
gap.checked_gap: Concrete and verifiable: Reflexion-style reflections are per-task and need retries at deployment, while cross-task persistent knowledge is missing. Fixed object changed: the agent's prompt context goes from a hand-written demonstration set to self-gathered, persisted insights plus retrieved own successes.
gap.lineage: ReAct (fixed few-shot) -> Reflexion (per-task retry memory) -> ExpeL (cross-task insights + retrieved successes); also generative-agents memory and Voyager skills named as related
gap.closest_adjacent: Reflexion (compared at R0-R3), generative agents memory (Park et al. 2023), Voyager (not compared); original papers not in the pinned materials, only the paper's description of them
gap.residue: Cross-task, no-retry knowledge retention; how to maintain a growing insight list
gap.stakes: API-only LLM agents cannot be tuned; few-shot demos are manually written
gap.method_response: Two retained stores built offline from contrast and success retrieval, applied with single-attempt inference
gap.remaining_gap: Insight retrieval/consolidation at scale (authors' limitation); insight admission not validated; actor limited to gpt-3.5; no evidence the loop improves the improver
unresolved: Memory/skill neighbours (Voyager, generative agents) are described by the paper only, not read; novelty beyond Reflexion is judged from the paper's own comparison.

matches.failure_checks: No contamination analysis for gpt-3.5/4 on benchmarks; single backbone

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: With gpt-3.5 as actor and a gpt-4 extractor, insights plus retrieved successes built on disjoint task halves improve single-attempt success over ReAct on HotpotQA (28->39) and ALFWorld (40->59) with modest WebShop gain, and removing either store loses part of the gain; one positive transfer pair to FEVER.
